 Coram:Honourable Mr. Justice Sandeep N. Bhatt
 Date : 12/09/2024
 Oral Order

1. The present First Appeal, under Section 173 of Motor Vehicles Act, 1988, is preferred by the appellant-GSRTC, being aggrieved and dissatisfied with the judgment and award dated 27.10.2023 passed by the Motor Accident Claims Tribunal, Vadodara in Motor Accident Claim Petition No.1423 of 2009, by which the Tribunal has awarded compensation of Rs.12,99,200/- with 9% per annum interest to the claimant/s, holding opponents liable jointly and severally.

entities.text: Motor Accident Claim Petition No.1423 of 2009
entities.label: CASE_NUMBER

sentences.text:
2. Brief facts of the case are as under:
2.1 The claimants filed the claim petition stating that on 17.2.2009, the deceased was travelling as pillion rider on Scooty No.GJ.06.CD.7475 driven by one Manjulaben Shersinh Vist who was driving her scooty at moderate speed on the NEUTRAL CITATION C/FA/3142/2024 ORDER DATED: 12/09/2024 undefined correct side of the road and at around 2.45 p.m. when they were passing by roses garden, they were hit by one ST bus No.GJ.18V.8606 driven by opponent no.1 rashly and negligently, as Gujarat State Road Transport ... vs Premnath Shambhuprasad Pandey on 12 September, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/52146624/
1

sentences.text: a result of which, the accident occurred and the deceased suffered injuries and she succumbed to the injuries on 30.8.2009.
Therefore, the claim petition was filed by the claimants.
2.2 Notices were served to the opponents.
Opponents appeared through their learned advocates and filed their written statement denying the contents of the claim petition.
The Tribunal has framed the issues.
The oral as well as documentary evidence were led by the rival parties before the Tribunal.
After considering the documentary as well as oral evidence and submissions made at the bar, the Tribunal has partly allowed the claim petition by awarding compensation as noted above.

2.3 Being aggrieved and dissatisfied with the impugned judgment and award passed by the Tribunal,
the present appeal is preferred by the appellant-GSRTC.

3. Learned advocate for the appellant-insurance company has assailed the impugned judgment and award on the sole ground of negligence and and submitted that looking to the NEUTRAL CITATION C/FA/3142/2024 ORDER DATED: 12/09/2024 undefined manner in which the accident occurred,
the driver of the ST bus cannot be held solely negligent; that no independent eye witnesses have been examined, no passengers in the bus were examined, and that the scooty driver was driving her scooty negligent and therefore she fell in the ditch and the ST bus driver cannot be held negligent for the same, however, the learned Tribunal has erred in holding the ST bus driver solely negligent for the accident.
4.

Further, though no arguments are advanced on the point of quantum, the said ground is raised in the memo of appeal to the effect that the age of the deceased was wrongly considered, the multiplier was wrongly applied, the income was wrongly considered by the learned Tribunal and the quantum awarded on other heads is also on higher side.
She, therefore, submitted to admit this appeal on both these counts.
5. I have considered the submissions made at the bar and also gone through the material produced on record, including the impugned judgment and award.

6. As regards the first contention of apportionment of negligence between the two vehicles, it is clear from the manner in which the accident occurred, as stated in the FIR NEUTRAL CITATION C/FA/3142/2024 ORDER DATED: 12/09/2024 undefined and panchanama, that the accident occurred when the ST bus dashed the scooty from behind.

The learned Tribunal has discussed the issue of negligence in paragraph no.12 to 14 by observing that the complaint was filed by the deceased herself, wherein she has unequivocally stated that she was travelling as a pillion rider on the scooty, and when they were passing by the spot of incident, one ST bus had dashed from behind with their scooty and as a result, they both fell down on the road and both of them sustained grievous injuries and that after the accident, the ST bus driver had fled away.

The joint written statement is filed by both the opponents, however, the opponent no.1 has not rebutted the evidence put forward by the claimants either by stepping into the witness box or by cross-examining the Gujarat State Road Transport ... vs Premnath Shambhuprasad Pandey on 12 September, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/52146624/
2 claimant no.2.

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
Therefore, the learned Tribunal had taken the adverse inference and held the opponent no.1 solely negligent for the accident, which is just and proper and not required to be interfered with, the FIR and panchanama also clearly establish the sole negligence of the ST bus driver and even it is expected that the ST bus being a bigger vehicle, should have taken care to avoid the accident.
7.
On the point of quantum, though grounds are raised in the appeal, no arguments are advanced by learned advocate for the appellant-GSRTC.

From the discussion made on the NEUTRAL CITATION C/FA/3142/2024 ORDER DATED: 12/09/2024 undefined point of quantum in the impugned judgment, in paragraphs nos. 5 to 27, the learned Tribunal has discussed each and every aspect relevant for arriving at just and proper compensation by considering the evidence led before it and the ratio laid down in various judgments of the Hon'ble Apex Court, which is just and proper and is not required to be interfered with in this appeal.
8. In view of the above, this appeal is required to be dismissed at the admission stage itself and therefore, the following order is passed.
9. In view of above, the following order is passed.
9.1 The present appeal is dismissed with no order as to costs.
Civil application also stands dismissed accordingly.

9.2 The amount lying with the Tribunal and/or in the FDR, if any, shall be disbursed to the claimant, along with accrued interest thereon if any, by account payee cheque, after proper verification and after following due procedure,
within a period of six weeks from today.
9.3 Record and proceedings be sent back to the concerned Tribunal, forthwith.
(SANDEEP N. BHATT,J)
